subject: Context footprint & $/1M token target — BrightRetail next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@brightretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Context footprint & $/1M token target — BrightRetail next steps

Hi Asha — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the asks we promised to send over from our call so your procurement and product teams have the numbers to evaluate: 

Call highlights (short):
- Primary product flows: personalized recommendations (search+rank), user-generated content assist (marketing copy + subject lines), and long-session history summarization for returns/customer service.
- Volume shape: heavy read/serve for recommendations, bursty generation for content assist, occasional multi-doc summarization requiring extended context.

Profile we captured (please confirm if any item below is off):
- Avg prompt tokens (mix-weighted): ~95 tokens (mostly metadata + short context for recs; higher for content assist).
- Avg completion tokens (mix-weighted): ~600 tokens.
- Usage split by feature (monthly traffic-weighted estimate): recommendations 55% (short completions), content assist 35% (longer completions), doc summarization 10% (long-context).
- Context-sizing needs (percent of calls): 8k windows required for ~82% of calls; 32k windows for ~15%; 128k windows for ~3% (legal/PO/returns deep history).
- Monthly token estimate (rough): prompts ~6M, completions ~18M — total ~24M tokens/month. (This is your working estimate; feel free to share production logs if you want us to re-profile.)

Pricing / unit economics conversation points:
- You mentioned a target unit cost: $700–$900 per 1M tokens for an initial pilot. For context, at 24M tokens/month that implies $16.8k–$21.6k/month on raw token pricing — excluding dedicated capacity or add-on observability.
- If you want a Dedicated/Committed option we can model a blended effective $/1M with reserved capacity + burst credits and a predictable latency SLA.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm that the monthly token estimate (24M) and context distribution above reflect what you expect in Q3.
2) Share a sample ~48-hour log or the sample payloads file (attached) so we can run a quick tokenization/profile and produce a per-feature token histogram.
3) If procurement wants to see a scoped 90-day pilot, we can draft a SOW (attached) with estimated spend and escalation path.
4) Proposed meeting: procurement + engineering deep-dive on Friday 5/28 at 10am PT — does that work for you?

Attachments: BrightRetail_sample_payloads.csv; BrightRetail_context_profile.xlsx; SOW-draft.pdf (all attached).

If any of the above numbers look off, flag them and I’ll rerun the profile. Happy to jump on a follow-up with your eng lead to walk through the tail distribution for 32k/128k requests.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0197
https://redwood.ai

---

Note: Attachments are stubs in this export: 
- BrightRetail_sample_payloads.csv (csv)
- BrightRetail_context_profile.xlsx (xlsx)
- SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Asha Mehta <asha@brightretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightRetail Procurement <procurement@brightretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Context footprint & $/1M token target — BrightRetail next steps

Thanks Tessa — this is a useful distillation. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) The % split looks roughly right. For the doc summarization flow the 128k need is mostly one-off (compliance/legal requests) — can you confirm that those would be billed differently (we expect longer KV/cache behavior and different throughput characteristics)?
2) On the unit cost target: procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a mid-point illustration (e.g., $800/1M) with and without Dedicated capacity (so we can compare against our internal cloud-run cost basis).
3) SLA: we need 99.9% availability and p95 latency targets for the recommendations path. Is that covered in the pilot SOW?

We can share a 48-hour sample of anonymized request logs by end of day tomorrow. If you can mock up the per-feature histogram and a simple cost model at $700/$800/$900 per 1M tokens that would be great.

Friday 5/28 10am PT is OK for a procurement + eng sync. If possible include an engineering rep who can speak to fallback models for 32k->8k.

— Asha
Head of AI Platform, BrightRetail
asha@brightretail.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Asha Mehta <asha@brightretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, BrightRetail Procurement <procurement@brightretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-26T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Context footprint & $/1M token target — BrightRetail next steps

Asha — thanks, quick responses inline and attaching a short model.

1) 128k billing & behavior: Long-context calls will be billed by tokens consumed in the usual way; operationally those requests are expensive because they hold larger KV caches and may drive a different kernel path. In the SOW we can call out a 128k add-on surcharge (we typically model as a 1.5x multiplier on unit token price for the small % of requests that use 128k to reflect node residency). We can also offer a pilot waiver to measure real cost with production traffic.

2) Mid-point illustration: attached is a one-page cost table at $700 / $800 / $900 per 1M tokens plus two scenarios: Hosted pay-as-you-go and Dedicated reserved baseline with 30% commit discount (numbers are illustrative — I flagged where we need the detailed log to refine). At your 24M tokens/month example, the $800 mid-point maps to ~$19.2k/month (token-only). With Dedicated/commit we can get effective $/1M down to ~$560 in that model, depending on commit size and burst policy.

3) SLA: The 90-day pilot SOW includes a 99.9% availability target for the recommendations route and a p95 latency objective; I'll have legal/ops confirm exact remediation terms.

Attachments included: short_cost_table.csv (one-line table), updated SOW-draft.pdf.

Next steps I’ll take before Friday:
- Run the attached tokenization script on any sample logs you send and produce a per-feature histogram.
- Karthik will review the fallback/32k->8k strategy with your eng team on Friday.

If procurement wants to see a conservative spend estimate for a 90-day pilot I can draft one (token-only + estimated infra uplift).

Best,
Tessa

---
Attachments (stubs): short_cost_table.csv (csv), updated SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-27T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: BrightRetail procurement + pilot — internal action items

Folks — forwarding the thread and our answers. Quick internal checklist before Friday: 
- Karthik: please prepare a 10–15 minute runbook on how we handle fallback from 32k to 8k models and the operational cost signals (KV cache warming, tail latency). Bring the latency graphs for p50/p95/p99.
- Ben: prep a rough pilot SOW cost table: token-only at $700/$800/$900 per 1M, plus a Dedicated reserved scenario with a 30% commit discount and a 128k surcharge of 1.5x for the small tail. Include a 90-day spend projection (token + infra uplift).
- Me: I’ll coordinate the Friday 10am PT invite and collect the anonymized log once Asha sends it.

Goal: have the procurement-ready model and SOW updated by EOD Thursday so procurement has something to review pre-meeting.

Thanks — Tessa

(Internal note: all internal participants are on this export and are Redwood employees.)
